title: Learning Multi-Timescale Abstractions for Hierarchical Combinatorial Planning
claim: A hierarchical agent plans over abstract subgoals and budgets with latent tree search, then a low-level policy executes them in the environment.
layout: 2 repeated columns (step 0, step k), top-down flow, environment bar at bottom
description: Two parallel columns show high-level steps 0 and k, joined by ellipses to imply repetition. Each column has a rounded light-green box labeled π^H. Inside, the state s enters an encoder h_θ, giving latent h_k. A tree-search diagram with a grey arrow for the value V^H branches downward. Below it are two bar charts: a blue search policy π_k and a green budget distribution b_ψ(·|h_k, z_k). A stacked colored block Z represents the subgoal space. The sampled subgoal and budget (z_k, b_k) fan out through curved arrows to several low-level π^L boxes, bounded by τ_k ≤ b_k. These boxes emit actions and receive next states through arrows to and from a grey Environment bar at the bottom. The eye goes first to the tree and the bar charts.
caption: Architecture of LMTA. At each high-level (HL) step, the planner encodes the state as hk and runs latent-space tree search over subgoals to produce a search policy πk(·). A subgoal zk is selected, after which the budget head samples bk, yielding HL action (zk, bk). The low-level (LL) policy πL executes primitive actions for τk steps to pursue zk, where τk ≤bk.
abstract: The combination of exponentially large action spaces, stochastic dynamics, and long-horizon decision-making under limited resources makes Sequential Stochastic Combinatorial Optimization (SSCO) particularly challenging for reinforcement learning. Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a natural decomposition, but it places the high-level policy in a Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP) where actions have variable durations, making it difficult to learn a world model that is suitable for planning. We introduce a model-based hierarchical framework for sequential stochastic combinatorial decision-making that directly addresses this issue. Our method combines a latent-space tree-search planner with an SMDP-aware world model for variable-duration decisions. A multi-timescale objective structures the latent dynamics so that transition magnitudes reflect the effective temporal scales of abstract actions, enabling efficient lookahead under adaptive temporal abstraction. We further learn a subgoal-conditioned budget policy jointly with the world model to support context-aware resource allocation. Across challenging SSCO benchmarks, our method outperforms strong baselines.
